name: Opening
purpose: Reach the right person and say who you are.
likely_statements: "Who is this? Which department are you looking for?"
"I am driving / in a meeting, who is calling?"
"He left the company a long time ago."
watch_out: Confirm the name before anything else. About 1 in 6 calls ends here.

name: Purpose
purpose: Say why you called in one or two sentences they can repeat to a colleague.
likely_statements: "What is this regarding? Which company are you from?"
"Where did you get my number?"
"Is this a sales call?"
quick_outcomes: Asked where we got the number
Said it is a sales call
watch_out: If they ask twice, the first answer was a label. Say it in plain words.

name: Permission
purpose: Find out whether they will talk now. A clear yes, a clear no or a time to call back are all good.
likely_statements: "Yes, go ahead." (then silence)
"Call me after two, or tomorrow."
"Send it on WhatsApp first."
watch_out: A short yes followed by silence is not permission. Wait for the actual answer.

name: Their business
purpose: Ask about their company and work before saying more about yours.
likely_statements: One line about what they do, then wait for the pitch.
"We do not make that. That is a different division."
"First tell me about your company."
watch_out: Callers often skip this stage. Ask one question about their work, then listen.

name: Their need, in their words
purpose: Hear what they are trying to do or struggling with. Write down exactly what was said.
likely_statements: A goal: a new market, a product line, better margins.
"Everything is fine, we do not need anything."
"What can you do for a company like ours?"
watch_out: Their words, not yours. The AI never overwrites this box.

name: Objection
purpose: Hear the reason for a no and understand it before answering.
likely_statements: "Send it in writing and we will see."
"Not me. Talk to our CFO or head office."
"We already have an internal team or consultant."
watch_out: Most objections are deflections (send it in writing, not me), not hard refusals. Deflections often still lead to a next step.

name: Next step
purpose: Agree one thing, named, with a channel or a time.
likely_statements: "Yes, send the document."
"Call me on Tuesday after two."
"Talk to my colleague, here is the number."
watch_out: A time they name is worth more than a time you propose. A yes to a document may be politeness.

name: Close
purpose: End clearly and record what happened.
likely_statements: The line drops mid-sentence.
A warm goodbye after a no, which is still a no.
"Okay, thank you." (after agreeing something)
watch_out: Record the outcome the words support, not the friendliest goodbye.
